mechanism_narrative: A high level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which is associated with positive equity market sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require a threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS is above 150,000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 3.5% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 295 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 3.0%, the combined signal of high inflation and restrictive monetary policy compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 295 AND FEDFUNDS > 3.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 295), a rise in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The mechanism is active only when CPIAUCSL exceeds 295.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 295 AND FEDFUNDS > 3.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand for residential construction, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive equity market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require a threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST is above 1400, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) signals a tight labor market, which is associated with strong consumer spending and positive equity market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 105 and housing starts (HOUST) exceeds 1400, the combined signal of strong industrial output and robust housing demand indicates a healthy economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO > 105 AND HOUST > 1400, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-demand regime (RSAFS > 650,000), a high level of retail sales (RSAFS) is associated with positive equity market sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The mechanism is active only when RSAFS exceeds 650,000.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS > 650000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
